title: Will the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee report more than $35M in cash on hand at the end of Q3? Above $35M
rules: If the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee's cash on hand is above $35 million as of September 30, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary: This market resolves based on the official filing data released by the Federal Election Commission (FEC). Only the first official or non-preliminary release of the relevant statistic will be used to resolve the market, and subsequent revisions, corrections, or updates will not affect resolution.

blind.reasoning: FEC data shows the DSCC's cash on hand falling from about $41.0M (June 30) to about $40M (July 31) to $37.6M (Aug 31), leaving only about $2.6M of room above $35M. In a competitive midterm, September usually brings a sharp rise in party-committee spending on fall ads and help for candidates, which tends to outpace strong end-of-quarter fundraising. Big September fundraising or large transfers in could still keep the balance above $35M.
blind.falsifier: The DSCC's September monthly report (due around Oct. 20) shows ending cash on hand above $35M, for example because record September fundraising or large joint-fundraising transfers outpaced fall ad spending.

final.reasoning: The market's 0.195 midpoint pulls me down from 0.35, since heavy September spending could easily erase the $2.6M cushion. But the wide spread and $37.6M at end of August still leave about a 1-in-4 chance, slightly above the 0.24 ask.
